# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✍]

I see a blue light, display `0`, the embossed warning “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE,” and three wires in order: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. The warning means Blind should not cut any wire unless the manual explicitly resolves that instruction. I am telling Mute the complete visual state so Mute can read the manual and relay the required action to Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see DISPLAY 0; LIGHT blue; embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires in order 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Read the manual for this exact state and tell Blind the required safe action, especially whether any wire must remain untouched.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see DISPLAY 0, LIGHT blue, and wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. The bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wait for Mute to read the manual and give the exact safe action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s thumbs-down gesture has no agreed meaning yet, so I cannot safely interpret it as an instruction. The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. I am asking Mute to use the manual and communicate the exact procedure aloud to Blind; Blind must not act on the ambiguous gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot safely interpret the thumbs-down without an agreed code. Please read the manual for DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue, then speak the exact safe procedure to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible state is unchanged. Do not act on the ambiguous thumbs-down gesture; wait for Mute's exact spoken manual instruction.")
```

LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. I still have no reliable meaning for Mute’s `✌` gesture, and gestures cannot reach Blind. Since Mute can read the manual and speak to Blind, I am again directing Mute to provide the exact action verbally rather than relying on an unagreed gesture code.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instruction to Blind now. Do not communicate the answer only by gesture; Blind cannot see gestures. State clearly whether to cut, press, or leave untouched, including any required wire number or order.")
speak(to="blind", text="The display, light, sign, and wires are unchanged. I have not received a reliable manual instruction. Do not cut or manipulate anything until Mute states the exact procedure aloud.")
```

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute continues to show `✌`, but no meaning for that gesture has been established; it cannot safely substitute for the manual’s spoken instruction to Blind. I am explicitly directing Mute to use speech for the actionable procedure and telling Blind to wait rather than infer an action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your repeated ✌ is not an established code. Speak the manual's exact actionable instruction to Blind now, including the control to use and any sequence. Do not rely on gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has shown me ✌, but that has no agreed meaning. Wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction; do not cut any wire.")
```

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s `[👇 ✌]` still has no agreed meaning, and gestures cannot convey an instruction to Blind. The only safe path is for Mute to read the manual and speak the exact procedure to Blind; until then, Blind should not touch the bomb.

```text

speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute's gestures are not a usable instruction. Do not touch or cut anything until Mute gives the exact manual procedure aloud.")
```

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute’s new gesture sequence `[🤏 ✌]` has no established meaning, and even a decoded gesture would not reach Blind. Mute must use speech to carry the manual’s answer to Blind, so I am directing that explicitly and warning Blind not to act on gestures.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot use [🤏 ✌] as an instruction because we established no gesture code. Speak the manual's exact procedure directly to Blind now, including whether every wire must remain untouched and what control, if any, to operate.")
speak(to="blind", text="The bomb remains DISPLAY 0, blue LIGHT, sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Ignore all gestures; wait for Mute's exact spoken manual instruction and do not touch the bomb.")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✌]

The bomb is unchanged. I now recognize that Mute cannot speak, so the manual’s answer must be conveyed by Mute’s gestures to me, then spoken by me to Blind. No gesture code was established, so `[👇 ✌]` is not yet safe to interpret. I am proposing a compact code and asking Mute to resend the complete instruction with it; Blind must wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I understand you cannot speak. Establish this code: 👍 means CUT, 👎 means DO NOT CUT, 👌 means PRESS or OPERATE, and wire numbers are ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. Send the complete manual instruction as action gesture followed by any wire-number gesture; use 🤚 to mean WAIT or no action. Resend it using only this code.")
speak(to="blind", text="I understand Mute cannot speak, so I must decode the manual through Mute's gestures and tell you aloud. No gesture code was established yet; do not act on [👇 ✌]. The bomb remains unchanged and no wire should be cut.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Blind gestures: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐]

Using the code I proposed, Mute’s `[👍 ✌]` means “CUT wire 2.” This conflicts with the printed warning, but Mute’s manual reading is the authoritative source for the procedure, so I must relay it precisely to Blind. Blind’s four gestures have no established meaning and do not alter the decoded instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Using the agreed code, Mute's instruction is: CUT wire 2, the green wire. This is the manual's instruction despite the printed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning. Your gestures [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐] have no established meaning. Cut wire 2 only.")
```
